title: Construct Process v1
description: A running plan, and the contract the Cockpit's Processes section renders. A process is an execution plan (schemas/plan.v1.json) plus everything the plan deliberately refuses to carry: which step is running, each step's status keyed by the plan step's `id`, a log whose every entry states whether a model was involved, and the files the process changed, collected for approval before anything is accepted. See src/engine/processMachine.mjs (the lifecycle, a real XState v5 config), src/engine/processModel.mjs (this record and its validator), src/engine/processStore.mjs (persistence) and src/engine/processEngine.mjs (the driver). test/processSchema.test.mjs asserts this file and the code never drift: every enum here is read out of the file and compared to the exported constant. DELIBERATE OMISSIONS: no step `status` is ever written back into the embedded plan (plan.v1.json rejects one, so re-planning the same ticket still produces byte-identical JSON), and nothing here is derived -- progress, model-step counts and available controls are computed by processSummary()/allowedEvents() rather than stored, so there is one source of truth. Additive data goes in the reserved free-form `ext` object, which validators ignore; any other unknown top-level field is rejected. A breaking change creates process.v2.json with a migrateProcess() step rather than mutating v1 in place (docs/VERSIONING.md).

version.description: Process schema version. Bump this file to v2 on any breaking shape change rather than mutating v1 in place.

id.description: Stable identifier for this run. Random by design: a process is an event in time, not a derivation of the plan, and two runs of the same plan are two processes.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path of the project this process runs against. Recorded inside the file as well as encoded in its directory name, so a state directory is readable by a human looking for which project a record belongs to.

title.description: What a list row shows. Defaults to the plan's ticket title.

plan.description: The execution plan being run, stored verbatim (schemas/plan.v1.json), so a process file read a week later still knows exactly what it was running even if the plan that produced it is gone.

state.description: The lifecycle state, as a resolved XState path. `running` is a compound state: `running.active` is executing steps, `running.stopping` means a pause or cancel has been asked for and the process is waiting for the step in flight to reach a yield point -- control is cooperative, since a step cannot be torn down mid-syscall. A UI showing six states takes the part before the dot; `done` and `cancelled` are final, while `failed` still accepts a retry.

pendingControl.description: A control the user asked for that has not taken effect yet. Set while the process is in `running.stopping`; it is what the guard on the YIELDED transition reads to decide whether the process settles into `paused` or `cancelled`.

currentStepId.description: The plan step id currently in flight, or awaiting the user.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp: when the process was created (not when it started).

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the START event, or null while queued.

finishedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of reaching done, failed or cancelled, or null.

error.description: A process-level failure -- the runtime itself stopping this process, as opposed to a step failing, which is recorded on the step.

ext.description: Reserved, free-form object for ADDITIVE data. Validators ignore its contents; any other unknown top-level field is still rejected (so typos are caught). See docs/VERSIONING.md.

pid.description: The OS process driving this one.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when it took ownership.

owner.description: Which OS process is driving this one, set whenever a `running` record is saved and cleared as soon as it stops. How a record left marked `running` by a killed server is recognised as not actually running: adoptInterrupted() moves such a record to `paused`, which is honest (it is not running) and offers the right affordance (resume).

steps.description: One entry per plan step, in plan order, keyed by the plan step's `id`. Run state lives here and never inside the plan.

log.description: What happened, oldest first. Bounded: the oldest entries are dropped past MAX_LOG_ENTRIES and counted in `logDropped`, so a long-running process cannot grow its state file without bound.

logSeq.description: The highest sequence number issued. Keeps increasing across dropped entries, so a streaming client can rely on never seeing the log go backwards.

logDropped.description: How many entries were dropped from the front of the log. Stated rather than hidden, so the log never pretends to be complete.

artifacts.description: The files this process changed, one entry per file, collected so the Diff tab can hold them for approval before anything is accepted. Only files that were actually written appear: a step whose changes failed validation wrote nothing and produces no artifact.

id.description: The plan step's id. This is the whole of the link between a plan and its run state.

flow.description: The plan flow this step runs, copied for display so a list does not have to index back into the plan.

status.description: `awaiting-user` is a `user`-executor step that has been reached: the process pauses and waits for the person, which is why a real `paused` state is needed rather than a boolean. `skipped` is a step that will never run, because the process was cancelled or something it depends on did not finish -- a step list must not leave such a step `pending` forever.

attempts.description: How many times this step has been started, including retries.

error.description: Why the step failed, or why it was skipped.

provider.description: Which provider was used, e.g. ollama.

llm.description: Whether a model was involved in this step. `null` means no model, and it is a recorded fact rather than an absent field: finishing a step without stating this is refused by the code, so "where did a model touch my project?" stays answerable for every step, including one that failed after calling a model.

provenance.description: The three badges docs/design/cockpit-layout.md section 5 names, and a closed set on purpose. `ok`: a deterministic block did this and it succeeded, with no model. `llm`: a model was involved, whatever the outcome -- keyed to involvement rather than success, so filtering to this one value always answers where a model touched the project. `warn`: something wants a human's attention, including a step failing. There is deliberately no separate `error` provenance: a failure is authoritatively `steps[].status === 'failed'` with `steps[].error`, not a log badge.

stepId.description: Which plan step produced this line, or null for a process-level line.

detail.description: Optional structured payload, e.g. the violations that stopped a commit. Free-form on purpose.

path.description: Project-relative path, the same rule the plan's `touches` follows, so a process record stays portable across machines.

change.description: A subset of the plan's touch changes: `read` and `move` are not artifacts, because nothing was written.

approved.description: The human verdict: null means collected but not yet decided. Starting at null is the point -- model output is collected, never accepted by default. Approving or rejecting without naming paths only touches artifacts still at null, so a bulk action cannot overturn a decision already made on one file.

sha256.description: sha256 of the content, or null when there was none (a created or deleted file).

blob.description: Size and hash of one side of the change, recorded when the caller supplied the content, so a Diff tab has something to check against without re-reading a tree that may have moved on.
